items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: what about Bill Evans? Not that they should have whole concerts or whatever, but just to get his opinion.

ctx.x: limited for black players. I mean there’s a lot of great black players from the 20s who like in the 30s were out of the music business and doing other things. So they had it rough. But the part that bothers me is just people who should be a little bit objective. I’m just bothered any time the focus is not on the music. Music should be judged on its own terms, not on racial terms. And I think one of the things I see happening is that jazz and the way it’s being marketed, by promoters, producers, club owners and…

there, as much as they deny it. And I’ve sat down and I’ve talked to Stanley Crouch, I know Stanley Crouch, I know Wynton Marsalis a little bit, I mean we’ve talked a couple of times. I think I’ve talked more in depth with Stanley Crouch. And like he says that it’s not a racial thing, like we just want to develop the jazz canon and just focus, and we can’t focus on Bix Beiderbecke until we’ve focused on all these other people and that’s great. But you happened to mention, well what about Benny Goodman or what…
